examples.dm: Establishing the highest joy, respect, and faith, Having cleared away the obscurations of the afflictions and transcended all stains, Listen to this perfection of wisdom of the noble ones, who are dedicated to the welfare of beings, And to that which is the conduct of the heroic ones.
examples.gm: Having established supreme joy, respect, and faith, Having removed obscurations and afflictions and passed beyond stains, The perfection of wisdom of the gentle ones engaged in the benefit of beings, Listen to that in which the heroes practice.
examples.sa: पर प्रेम गौरव प्रसाद उपस्थपित्वा प्रजहित्व आवरण क्लेशमलातिक्रान्ताः । शृणुता जगार्थमभिप्रस्थित सुरव्रतानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति शूराः ॥

examples.dm: Just as seeds that are sown and remain in the earth will eventually grow, Once the assembly of conditions is found, diverse forms are fully produced; The five perfections and however many qualities of awakening there are, All of them are born from the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Seeds, having been sown and resting in the earth, will arise; Having found the proper conditions, many kinds of forms are fully produced. The five perfections and however many qualities of awakening there are, All of them also are produced from the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: बीजाः प्रकीर्ण पृथिवीस्थित संभवन्ति सामग्रि लब्ध्व विरुहन्ति अनेकरुपाः । यावन्ति बोधिगुण पारमिताश् च पञ्च प्रज्ञाय पारमित ते विरुहन्ति सर्वे ॥

examples.dm: Whoever practices here does not conceptualize the Buddha-qualities, Nor do they conceptualize the powers, the bases of miraculous power, awakening, or peace. They practice through the blessing of non-conceptuality, free from mental construction; This is the practice of the supreme Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: Whoever practices here does not conceptualize the qualities of a Buddha; They do not conceptualize the powers, the bases of miraculous power, or peaceful enlightenment; Non-conceptualizing and free from concepts, they practice through blessing; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: चरमाणु यो न इह कल्पयि बुद्धधर्मां बल ऋद्धिपाद न च कल्पयि बोधि शान्ताम् । अविकल्पकल्पविगतोऽधिष्ठानचारी एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: If one gives rise to the perception of sentient beings or the perception of suffering, Thinking, "I shall act for the benefit of beings and eliminate their suffering," One is a bodhisattva who conceptualizes a self and sentient beings; This is not the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: If they generate the perception of sentient beings and the perception of suffering, Thinking, "I shall act for the benefit of beings and eliminate their suffering," They are a bodhisattva who conceptualizes self and sentient beings; This is not the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: सचि सत्त्वसंज्ञ दुखसंज्ञ उपादयाती हरिष्यामि दुःख जगतीं करिष्यामि अर्थम् । सो आत्मस(त्त्व) परिकल्पकु बोधिसत्त्वो न च एष प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: The Perfection of Wisdom is the pleasure grove where they abide; It is the sphere of activity for the Guides who possess the ten powers. Although they completely deliver sentient beings from the sufferings of the three lower realms, They never entertain the notion of a "sentient being."
examples.gm: Relying on the perfection of wisdom as a pleasure grove, This is the domain of the guides with the ten powers; Even though they fully extract sentient beings from the suffering of the three lower realms, They never have the notion of "sentient beings".
examples.sa: अयु गोचरो दशबलान विनायकानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित रम्यवनाश्रितानाम् । दुखितांश्च सत्त्व त्रिअपाय समुद्धरन्ति न पि सत्त्वसंज्ञ अपि तेषु कदाचि भोति ॥

examples.dm: Just as a person who finds a supreme jewel they had never found before, Is filled with joy at having found it at another time, If they become careless and lose it immediately after finding it, They will suffer constant longing for the jewel they have lost.
examples.gm: A person who previously had not found a supreme jewel, Finding it at another time, out of joy, If they lose it right after finding it by becoming careless, By losing it, desiring the jewel, they will constantly suffer.
examples.sa: पुरुषो य अग्रु रतनस्य अलब्धपूर्वो अपरस्मि कालि पुन लब्ध्व भवेय तुष्टो । स ह लब्ध्व नाशयि पुनोऽपि प्रमादभूतो नाशित्व दुःखि सततं रतनाभिकाङ्क्षी ॥

examples.dm: The wise and learned Bodhisattva who practices in this way, Does not train in the stage of an Arhat, nor in the stage of a Pratyekabuddha; For the sake of omniscience, they train following the Buddha-dharma. One who does not train in the distinction between training and non-training is one who trains.
examples.gm: A wise, understanding bodhisattva who practices in this way Does not train for the level of an arhat, nor the level of a pratyekabuddha; For the sake of omniscience itself, they train in the qualities of a buddha; Whoever does not train in training and no-more-training, that is training.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्तु विदु पण्डितु बोधिसत्त्वो नार्हंमि शिक्षति न प्रत्ययबुद्धभूमौ । सर्वज्ञताय अनुशिक्षति बुद्धधर्मे शिक्षाअशिक्ष न य शिक्षति एष शिक्षा ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, in this case as well, without the mind of enlightenment, How could the primordial wisdom of the Sugatas ever arise throughout all these worlds? Without primordial wisdom, there is no increase in qualities and no enlightenment; Even the ocean-like qualities of a Buddha would also not exist.
examples.gm: Likewise, here too, without the mind of awakening, how could The pristine knowledge of the Sugata emerge in all these worlds? Without pristine knowledge, there is no increase of qualities and no awakening, And the buddha-dharmas, which are like the ocean, would also not exist.
examples.sa: तथ बोधिचित्त असतीह तथागतस्य कुत ज्ञानप्रस्रवु भवेदिह सर्वलोके । ज्ञानस्य चो असति नास्ति गुणान वृद्धिः न च बोधि सागरसमा न च बुद्धधर्माः ॥

examples.dm: From the time they first generate the aspiration for supreme enlightenment, Until the time the true Dharma of those guides is exhausted, Whatever merit those Victors possess during that interval, Including the perfections and all the Buddha-qualities,
examples.gm: From when they first generated the mind for supreme awakening, Until the time the holy dharma of those Guides is exhausted, Whatever merit those Victors have during that time, And whatever is endowed with the perfections and whatever buddha-dharmas—
examples.sa: प्रथमं उपादु वरबोधयि चित्तुपादो यावत् सु धर्मक्षयकालु विनायकानाम् । एकस्मि तत्र चिय तेष जिनान पुण्यं सह युक्त पारमित येऽपि च बुद्धधर्माः ॥

examples.dm: And whatever virtues—both contaminated and uncontaminated— Of the Buddha’s sons, the śrāvakas, those in training, and those beyond training, The bodhisattva gathers together and rejoices in, And dedicates it all toward enlightenment for the sake of the welfare of beings.
examples.gm: And whatever [virtues] of the sons of the buddhas, and the śrāvakas, The virtues of learners and non-learners, with defilements and without defilements, Having gathered them, the bodhisattva rejoices, And dedicates them all for the sake of awakening, as a cause for the benefit of wandering beings.
examples.sa: यश् चैव बुद्धतनयान(च) श्रावकाणां शैक्ष अशैक्ष कुशलास्रव नास्रवाश्च । परिपिण्डयित्व अनुमोदयि बोधिसत्त्वो सर्वं च नामयि जगार्थनिदान बोधि ॥

examples.dm: If one understands that these phenomena have ceased and are exhausted, And that which is dedicated is also exhausted, And that a phenomenon never dedicates to a phenomenon, Then by knowing in such a way, it is a perfect dedication.
examples.gm: If in this way one knows that this dharma has ceased and is exhausted, And that to which it is dedicated is also exhausted, And knows that a dharma is never dedicated to a dharma, Through knowing in that way, it is perfectly dedicated.
examples.sa: सचि एव जानति निरुध्यति क्षीणधर्मा तच्चैत क्षीण परिणामयिष्यन्ति यत्र । न च धर्म धर्मि परिणामयते कदाचित् परिणामितं भवति एव प्रजानमाने ॥

examples.dm: If one conceives of it in terms of signs, that is not a dedication. If there are no signs, that is the dedication to enlightenment. Just as eating fine food that has been mixed with poison, The Victor has taught that focusing on virtuous qualities is the same.
examples.gm: If one acts upon signs, that is not dedication; But if there are no signs, it is dedication to awakening. Just like eating excellent food mixed with poison, The Victor has declared that apprehending white dharmas is like that.
examples.sa: सचि सो निमित्त कुरुते न च मानयाति अथ आनिमित्त परिणामित भोन्ति बोधौ । विषसृष्ट भोजनु यथैव क्रियाप्रणीतो तथ शुक्लधर्मौपलम्भ जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: If, while lacking such knowledge, one perceives form, And engages with the aggregates of feeling, volition, and consciousness, Even if one conceptualizes that "these aggregates are empty," that bodhisattva Is still practicing with signs and lacks faith in the state of non-arising.
examples.gm: If, lacking understanding, one perceives form, And practices regarding the aggregates of feeling, volition, and consciousness, Even if they think "these aggregates are empty," the bodhisattva Practices in signs, and does not have faith in the unborn state.
examples.sa: सचि रुप संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतना च विज्ञान स्कन्ध चरती अप्रजानमानो । इमि स्कन्ध शून्य परिकल्पयि बोधिसत्त्वो चरती निमित्तअनुपादपदे असक्तो ॥

examples.dm: If one conceives of it in terms of signs, that is not a dedication. If there are no signs, that is the dedication to enlightenment. Just as eating fine food that has been mixed with poison, The Victor has taught that focusing on virtuous qualities is the same.
examples.gm: If one acts upon signs, that is not dedication; But if there are no signs, it is dedication to awakening. Just like eating excellent food mixed with poison, The Victor has declared that apprehending white dharmas is like that.
examples.sa: सचि सो निमित्त कुरुते न च मानयाति अथ आनिमित्त परिणामित भोन्ति बोधौ । विषसृष्ट भोजनु यथैव क्रियाप्रणीतो तथ शुक्लधर्मौपलम्भ जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: While practicing the dharmas of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, They do not touch upon nirvāṇa, yet do not engage in signs; For example, just as a skilled boatman goes back and forth, Without staying on either shore and without remaining in the ocean.
examples.gm: Practicing the dharmas of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, Not touching nirvāṇa and not engaging in signs, Just as a skilled boatman going back and forth, Does not dwell on either shore, nor does he dwell in the ocean.
examples.sa: शून्यानिमित्तप्रणिधिं चरमाणु धर्मा न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति नो च निमित्तचारी । यथ नाविको कुशल गच्छति आरपारम् उभयान्ति अस्थितु न तिष्ठति अर्णवेस्मिन् ॥

examples.dm: And whatever virtues—both contaminated and uncontaminated— Of the Buddha’s sons, the śrāvakas, those in training, and those beyond training, The bodhisattva gathers together and rejoices in, And dedicates it all toward enlightenment for the sake of the welfare of beings.
examples.gm: And whatever [virtues] of the sons of the buddhas, and the śrāvakas, The virtues of learners and non-learners, with defilements and without defilements, Having gathered them, the bodhisattva rejoices, And dedicates them all for the sake of awakening, as a cause for the benefit of wandering beings.
examples.sa: यश् चैव बुद्धतनयान(च) श्रावकाणां शैक्ष अशैक्ष कुशलास्रव नास्रवाश्च । परिपिण्डयित्व अनुमोदयि बोधिसत्त्वो सर्वं च नामयि जगार्थनिदान बोधि ॥

examples.dm: Therefore, one should train in dedication in this way: Whatever the nature, the source, and the characteristics of that virtue Are as known by those Victors, One should rejoice in it and dedicate it in exactly that same way.
examples.gm: Therefore, one should train in dedicating in this way: Just as those Victors know that virtue— Whatever its aspect, whatever its origin, whatever its defining characteristic— Rejoicing in it, one perfectly dedicates it in exactly that way.
examples.sa: तस्मा हु नामपरिणामन शिक्षितव्या यथ ते जिना कुशल एव प्रजानयन्ति । यज्जातियोऽयं प्रभवो यदलक्षणं च अनुमोदमी तथ तथा परिणामयामि ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who meditates on the supreme perfection of wisdom, And having arisen from that, teaches the stainless Dharma, And dedicates that for the sake of beings as the cause of enlightenment— There is no virtue in the three worlds equal to that.
examples.gm: Any bodhisattva who meditates on the supreme wisdom, Arising from that, teaches the untainted dharma, And dedicates that as a cause for awakening for the sake of beings, There is no virtue equal to that in the three worlds.
examples.sa: यो बोधिसत्त्व वरप्रज्ञ विभावयन्तो तत उत्थितो कथयि धर्म निरुपलेपम् । तं चापि नामयि जगार्थनिदान बोधौ नास्ति त्रिलोक शुभ तेन समं भवेया ॥

examples.dm: Yet someone were to write down in a book this Mother of the Sugatas, From whom the Ten Powers of the Guides arise, And, bearing it, were to honor it with flowers and ointments, The merit of having worshiped stūpas would not approach even a fraction of that.
examples.gm: Whoever, regarding that from which the Guides of ten powers will arise, Writes this Mother of the Sugatas in a book, Retains it, and pays reverence with flowers and ointments, The merit of building stūpas and making offerings cannot match a fraction of that.
examples.sa: यश् चो इमां सुगतमात लिखित्व पुस्ते यत उत्पती दशबलान विनायकानाम् । धारेयि सत्करयि पुष्पविलेपनेहि कल पुण्य भोन्ति न स स्तूपि करित्व पूजाम् ॥

examples.dm: A bodhisattva practicing in this way has no conceit, thinking, "I will be prophesied by the Ten-Powered Ones and shall reach enlightenment." Thinking, "There is nothing at all here," they have no fear of enlightenment. To practice in such a manner is to practice the wisdom of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: A bodhisattva practicing in this way has no conceited mind thinking, "I Am prophesied by the Ten-Powered One and will touch awakening," Nor do they fear awakening, thinking, "There is nothing at all here"; Practicing in this way is practicing the wisdom of the sugatas.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्तु न च मन्यति बोधिसत्त्वो अहु व्याकृतो दशबलेहि स्पृशेय बोधिम् । न च त्रासु बोधि भवते न इहास्ति किंचिद् एवं चरन्तु चरती सुगतान प्रज्ञाम् ॥

examples.dm: The Perfection of Wisdom is the pleasure grove where they abide; It is the sphere of activity for the Guides who possess the ten powers. Although they completely deliver sentient beings from the sufferings of the three lower realms, They never entertain the notion of a "sentient being."
examples.gm: Relying on the perfection of wisdom as a pleasure grove, This is the domain of the guides with the ten powers; Even though they fully extract sentient beings from the suffering of the three lower realms, They never have the notion of "sentient beings".
examples.sa: अयु गोचरो दशबलान विनायकानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित रम्यवनाश्रितानाम् । दुखितांश्च सत्त्व त्रिअपाय समुद्धरन्ति न पि सत्त्वसंज्ञ अपि तेषु कदाचि भोति ॥

examples.dm: For example, consider a man who indulges in desire and, Having made an appointment with a woman, fails to meet her; However many conceptual thoughts he experiences in his mind throughout a single day, For that many eons, the bodhisattva will achieve attainment.
examples.gm: For example, a man who engages in the phenomena of desire, Having made an appointment with a woman and not meeting her, However many discursive thoughts of his mind operate in a single day, The bodhisattva will gain that many eons.
examples.sa: यथ रागधर्मचरितः पुरुषः स्त्रियाये संकेत कृत्व अलभन्तु विवर्तयेया । यावन्ति चित्तचरिता दिवसेन तस्य तावन्त कल्प अनुबुध्यति बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: It is taught that the way one grasps is the way one is completely afflicted; It is said that when "I" and "mine" are not observed, there is total purification. In this, without anything being defiled or purified, The Bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Just as there is apprehension, so is complete affliction taught; Not apprehending self and what belongs to self is taught as complete purification; In this, without anything becoming afflicted or completely pure, The bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यथ उद्ग्रहो तथ प्रकाशितु संकिलेशो व्योदान उक्त अहु मह्य अनोपलब्धि । न हि अत्र कश्चि यो क्लिश्यति शुध्यते वा प्रज्ञाय पारमित बुध्यति बोधिसत्त्वे ॥

examples.dm: Even a massive heap of ordinary glass trinkets Is outshone by a single precious lapis lazuli gem; Likewise, all the vast heaps of generosity of all beings Are outshone by a bodhisattva who rejoices.
examples.gm: Even a great heap of imitation glass jewels Is completely outshone by a single precious lapis lazuli; Likewise, all the vast heaps of giving of all beings Are outshone by the rejoicing bodhisattva.
examples.sa: काचस्य वा मणिन राशि सिया महन्तो वैडूर्यरत्न अभिभोति स सर्व एको । एमेव सर्वजगती पृथु दानस्कन्धो अभिभोति सर्वपरिणामकु बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: Just as seeds that are sown and remain in the earth will eventually grow, Once the assembly of conditions is found, diverse forms are fully produced; The five perfections and however many qualities of awakening there are, All of them are born from the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Seeds, having been sown and resting in the earth, will arise; Having found the proper conditions, many kinds of forms are fully produced. The five perfections and however many qualities of awakening there are, All of them also are produced from the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: बीजाः प्रकीर्ण पृथिवीस्थित संभवन्ति सामग्रि लब्ध्व विरुहन्ति अनेकरुपाः । यावन्ति बोधिगुण पारमिताश् च पञ्च प्रज्ञाय पारमित ते विरुहन्ति सर्वे ॥

examples.dm: How could billions of blind people, lacking a guide, Ever know the path or enter the city? Without wisdom, these five perfections are sightless; Lacking a guide, they are unable to reach enlightenment.
examples.gm: Hundreds of billions of blind people without a guide, Not even knowing the way, how could they enter the city? Without wisdom, these five blind perfections, Being without a guide, are unable to touch awakening.
examples.sa: जात्यन्धकोटिनियुतान्यविनायकानां मार्गे अकोविदु कुतो नगरप्रवेशे । विन प्रज्ञ पञ्च इमि पारमिता अचक्षुः अविनायका न प्रभवन्ति स्पृशेतु बोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: In the same way, these five perfections of the Victors Also acquire the very name of the perfection of wisdom. When they are fully dedicated for the sake of omniscience, All these six become of one taste, known as "awakening."
examples.gm: Likewise, these five perfections of the Victors also Will attain the very name of the perfection of wisdom. When fully dedicated for the sake of omniscience, All these six become of one taste, called awakening.
examples.sa: एमेव पञ्च इमि पारमिता जिनानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित नामतया भवन्ति । सर्वज्ञताय परिणामयमाण सर्वे षडपीह एकनयम् अर्छति बोधिनामा ॥

examples.dm: Even if these five perfections of the Victors were practiced For many tens of billions of eons, And one constantly relied upon infinite and vast aspirations within the world, Without skillful means and separated from wisdom, one falls into the level of a śrāvaka.
examples.gm: Even if these five perfections of the Victors Have been accomplished for many koṭis of niyutas of eons, And one has constantly relied on the world with boundless, vast aspirations, Lacking skillful means and devoid of wisdom, one will fall into the level of a śrāvaka.
examples.sa: यद्य् आपि पञ्च इम पारमिता जिनानां बहुकल्पकोटिनियुतां समुदानयेय्या । प्रणिधीननन्तविपुलां सद सेव्य लोके अनुपाय प्रज्ञविकला परि श्रावकत्वे ॥

examples.dm: If, in a dream, one sees sentient beings dwelling in the three lower realms, And in that very moment makes a prayer to cut the continuum of the lower realms, And pacifies a mass of fire through the power of the blessing of truth— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: In a dream, seeing sentient beings abiding in the three lower realms, In that instant they make aspirations to cut off the stream of the lower realms. Through the blessing of truth, the masses of fire are pacified; They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.
examples.sa: त्रि-अपायप्राप्तु सुपिनस्मि विदित्व सत्त्वान् प्रणिधेति तत्क्षण अपाय उच्छोषयेयम् । सत्याधिष्ठानि प्रशमेति स चाग्निस्कन्धम् अविवर्तियेति अयु व्याकृतु वेदितव्यो ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, a bodhisattva who abides in emptiness, Through aspirations based on the knowledge of sentient beings in the world, Manifests a great variety of diverse activities, Yet does not touch upon nirvana, nor do they remain in emptiness.
examples.gm: Likewise, a bodhisattva dwelling in emptiness, Supported by aspirations knowing sentient beings among wanderers, Demonstrates many various kinds of activities, Does not touch nirvāṇa, and does not dwell in emptiness.
examples.sa: एमेव शून्यतप्रतिष्ठितु एष सत्त्वो जगति क्रियां विविध दर्शयते विचित्राम् । सत्त्वान ज्ञानप्रणिधानअधिष्ठानमेव न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति शून्यत नास्ति स्थानम् ॥

examples.dm: If one wishes to attain the awakening of an Arhat or a Pratyekabuddha, One is immoral, unskilled, and one’s conduct has degenerated. But if one fully dedicates toward supreme, peaceful awakening, Even while engaged in sensory pleasures, one abides in the perfection of ethical discipline.
examples.gm: If one desires to touch the awakening of an arhat or solitary realizer, One's discipline is broken, one is unwise, and thus one's conduct degenerates. But if one completely dedicates it to the supreme, peaceful awakening, Even while engaged in sensory pleasures, one abides in the perfection of discipline.
examples.sa: सचि प्रत्ययानरहबोधि स्पृहां जनेति दुःशील भोति विदुषां तथ छिद्रचारी । अथ बोधि उत्तमशिवां परिणामयन्ति स्थितु शीलपारमित कामगुणेभि युक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Those qualities from which the virtues of certain awakening arise— This is the meaning of ethical discipline for those endowed with virtuous qualities. The complete degeneration of the awakening of those who perform beneficial dharmas— This is what the Guide has called "immoral conduct."
examples.gm: Whatever dharmas produce the qualities of definite awakening, This is the purpose of discipline for those endowed with virtuous dharmas. Whatever dharmas cause the awakening of benefactors to completely degenerate, This was taught by the Guide to be broken discipline.
examples.sa: यो धर्म बोधिगुणआगमु सूरतानां सो शीलअर्थु गुणधर्मसमन्वितानाम् । यो धर्म बोधिगुणहानि हितंकराणां दुःशीलता अयु प्रकाशितु नायकेन ॥

examples.dm: If a bodhisattva practicing the path of the Victors thinks, "These sentient beings are ethical, but those are unethical," Engaging in such diverse perceptions, they are utterly lacking in ethical discipline; Their morality has degenerated, and they lack completely purified morality.
examples.gm: If a bodhisattva practicing the path of the Victorious Ones Thinks, "These sentient beings have discipline; these have broken discipline," By engaging in such diverse perceptions, their discipline is completely broken; Their discipline degenerates, and they lack completely pure discipline.
examples.sa: यदि बोधिसत्त्व चरमाणु जिनान मार्गे इमि शीलवानिमि दुशील करोति सत्त्वान् । नानात्वसंज्ञप्रसृतो परमं दुशीलो अपि छिद्रशीलु न तु सो परिशुद्धशीलो ॥

examples.dm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness; One does not dwell in the attainment of the fruit or the stage of an arhat, Nor does one dwell in the stage of a pratyekabuddha or likewise the stage of a buddha.
examples.gm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, attractive and unattractive, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness, Attaining the fruit, and not abiding in the level of an arhat, Not abiding in the level of a pratyekabuddha, and likewise not in the level of a buddha.
examples.sa: नित्यम् अनित्यसुखदुःखशुभाशुभं ति आत्मन्य् अनात्मि तथता तथ शून्यतायाम् । फलप्राप्तिताय अथितो अरहन्तभूमौ प्रत्येकभूमिस्थितो तथ बुद्धभूमौ ॥

examples.dm: Those who engage in the practice of benefit and compassion, Having trained in this vidyā-mantra, the wise shall touch enlightenment; One should know that all forms of happiness, Whether conditioned or unconditioned, arise from this.
examples.gm: Those who practice the practices endowed with benefit and compassion, The wise ones, having trained in this mantra, will touch awakening. Whatever is conditioned happiness and unconditioned happiness, One should know that all those forms of happiness arise from this.
examples.sa: ये वा चरन्ति चरियां हितसानुकम्पाम् इह विद्यशिक्षित विदु स्पृशिष्यन्ति बोधिम् । ये सौख्य संस्कृत असंस्कृत ये च सौख्या सर्वे च सौख्य प्रसुता इतु वेदितव्याः ॥

examples.dm: Suppose someone were to make offerings to the stūpas Of the Sugatas who have passed into parinirvāṇa, constructing them of the seven precious gems, And were to fill a thousand million buddha-fields With as many stūpas of the Sugatas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges;
examples.gm: If someone, of the completely parinirvāṇized Sugata, Were to build stūpas from the seven precious things and make offerings, and with those stūpas of the Sugata, as numerous as the Ganges' Sands, were to fill thousands of millions of fields;
examples.sa: परिनिर्वृतस्य सुगतस्य करेय्य स्तूपां पूजेय सप्तरतनामयु कश्चिद् एव । तेहि प्रपूर्ण सिय क्षेत्रसहस्रकोट्यो यथ गङ्गवालिकसमैः सुगतस्य स्तूपैः ॥

examples.dm: On whichever path a universal monarch constantly travels, On that very path, the seven precious jewels and all the military hosts follow; Wherever this Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors goes, From that very place, all the qualities and dharmas will follow.
examples.gm: Whichever path a Universal Monarch always travels upon, By that very path, the seven precious things and all the troops proceed. Wherever this perfection of wisdom of the Victors goes, Along that very path, all qualities and dharmas will go.
examples.sa: येनैव राज व्रजते स ह चक्रवर्ती तेनैव सप्त रतना बलकाय सर्वे । येनैव प्रज्ञ इय पारमिता जिनानां तेनैव सर्वगुणधर्म समागमन्ति ॥

examples.dm: Teaching of the knowledge of all bases
examples.gm: Teaching on the Knowledge of All Bases

examples.dm: The third chapter teaches the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, the heroic practitioners Truly transcend the three realms, yet they do not enter a narrow liberation. Although they have eliminated the afflictions, they manifest birth; Although they are free from aging, sickness, and death, they manifest passing away.
examples.gm: The third chapter: teaching the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, wherever the hero practices, They completely transcend the three realms, yet are not liberated; Though afflictions are cleared away, they display birth; Though without aging, sickness, and death, they display death and transmigration.
examples.sa: त्रैधातुकं समतिक्रान्त न बोधिसत्त्वा क्लेशापनीत उपपत्ति निदर्शयन्ति । जरव्याधिमृत्युविगताश् च्युति दर्शयन्ति प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति धीराः ॥

examples.dm: Those of great renown don the armor of difficult deeds, Which is not the armor of the aggregates, elements, and sense sources. They are free from the concept of the three vehicles and have no grasping; They are irreversible, unwavering, and possess the quality of being imperturbable.
examples.gm: Those endowed with great renown don the armor that is difficult to do; It is not the armor of the aggregates, elements, or sense bases. They are free from the perception of the three vehicles and have no grasping. They are irreversible, unwavering, and of unperturbed nature.
examples.sa: संनाहु दुष्करू महायशु संनहन्ती न च स्कन्धधातु न च आयतनैः सनद्धाः । त्रिभि यानसंज्ञविगता अपरिगृहीता अविवर्तिका अचलिताश्च अकोप्यधर्माः ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who has become profound in that way, And who realizes this Dharma—the ultimate, unattached vehicle in which aggregates, Elements, and sense sources do not exist— What could there be that is a more perfect accomplishment of merit than that?
examples.gm: For any bodhisattva who realizes this profound Vehicle, ultimate and unattached, wherein the aggregates, Elements, and sense-sources do not exist— What perfectly accomplished merit is there beyond that?
examples.sa: यो बोधिसत्त्व इमु बुध्यति एव धर्मां गम्भीरयानपरमार्थनिरुपलेपान् । यस्मिन् न स्कन्ध न पि आयतनं न धातु किं वा स्वपुण्यसमुदागमु किंचि तस्य ॥

examples.dm: For example, just as those who desire jewels go to a jewel island, And having found jewels, return home again, They do not live in happiness there as solitary captains, While leaving their circle of kinsmen and friends in misery.
examples.gm: For example, a person desiring jewels, having gone to a jewel island, And having found jewels, returns home again; Just as that merchant does not merely live happily by himself there, And leave his host of relatives and friends unhappy.
examples.sa: रतनार्थिको यथ व्रजित्वन रत्नद्वीपं लब्ध्वान रत्न पुन गेहम् उपागमेय्या । किंचापि तत्र सुख जीवति सार्थवाहो अपि दुःखितो मनसि भोति स जातिसंघो ॥

examples.dm: For example, in order to gain knowledge of the route, a merchant seeking profit Travels to whatever cities, towns, or villages lie along the way; He does not remain there, nor does he remain even on the Island of Jewels, And without staying at home, he becomes an expert on the path.
examples.gm: For example, an ambitious merchant, in order to know the routes, Goes to whatever intermediate cities, towns, and villages there are. He does not dwell there, nor does he dwell on the jewel island; The wise one does not dwell at home, but becomes skilled in the path.
examples.sa: अभ्यन्तरे य नगरे निगमे च ग्रामे कामार्थ वाणिजु यथा गमि जाननाय । नो चापि तत्र स्थिहती न च रत्नद्वीपे न च गेह मार्गि कुशलो पुन भोति विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: However many sentient beings there are—the lesser, the middling, and the superior— The Sugata taught that they all arise from ignorance. When conditions assemble, the machine of suffering fully emerges; That machine of ignorance neither exhausts nor increases.
examples.gm: However many inferior, middling, and supreme sentient beings there are, The Sugatas have taught that they all arise from ignorance; When conditions come together, the machine of suffering perfectly arises, Yet that machine of ignorance has no exhaustion and no increase.
examples.sa: यावन्त सत्त्व मृदुमध्यमुत्कृष्ट लोके सर्वे अविद्यप्रभवा सुगतेन उक्ताः । सामग्रिप्रत्ययु प्रवर्तति दुःखयन्त्रो न च यन्त्र क्षीयति अविद्य न चापि वृद्धिः ॥

examples.dm: However many aspects of primordial wisdom, gateways, methods, and roots there may be, All these arise from the supreme Perfection of Wisdom. When conditions assemble, the machine of karma fully emerges; In the Perfection of Wisdom, there is no exhaustion and no increase.
examples.gm: However many approaches to knowledge, methods, and roots there are, They all arise from the supreme perfection of wisdom; When conditions come together, the machine of activities perfectly arises, Yet the perfection of wisdom has no exhaustion and no increase.
examples.sa: यावन्ति ज्ञान नयद्वार उयायमूलाः सर्वे ति प्रज्ञवरपारमिताप्रसूताः । सामग्रिप्रत्यय प्रवर्तति ज्ञानयन्त्रो न च प्रज्ञपारमित वर्धति हीयते वा ॥

examples.dm: Teaching of the gradual path
examples.gm: Teaching on the Gradual Approach

examples.dm: The sixth chapter explains the gradual path. Through the generosity of a bodhisattva, the path to the realm of hungry spirits is cut off; It likewise eliminates poverty and all afflictions. When practiced, one will obtain an infinite expansion of resources; Through generosity, one brings sentient beings who are suffering to full maturity.
examples.gm: Chapter Six: Teaching the Gradual Training. By the bodhisattva's giving, the destiny of hungry ghosts is cut off; Poverty and likewise all afflictions are cut off; While practicing, they will obtain infinite, abundant wealth, And by giving, they fully ripen sentient beings who are suffering.
examples.sa: दानेन प्रेतगति छिन्दति बोधिसत्त्वो दारिद्रकं च छिनती तथ सर्वक्लेशान् । भोगांश् चनन्तविपुलां लभते चरन्तो दानेन सत्त्व परिपाचयि कृच्छ्रप्राप्तान् ॥

examples.dm: The first chapter teaches omniscience of all aspects. Whatever rivers flow here in Jambudvīpa, Producing flowers, fruits, medicinal plants, and forests, All depend upon the Naga King, the Lord of Nagas, who dwells in Anavatapta; They are the power and glory of that Lord of Nagas.
examples.gm: Chapter One: The Teaching on the Knowledge of All Aspects. However many rivers flow in this Jambudvīpa, Producing flowers, fruits, medicinal herbs, and forests, All depend upon the nāga king, the lord of nāgas, dwelling in Anavatapta; It is the majestic power of that lord of nāgas.
examples.sa: यावन्ति नद्य प्रवहन्ति ह जम्बुद्वीपे फल पुष्प औषधाधि वनस्पति रोहयन्ति । भूजत गजेन्द्रनागपतिनिश्रयनोवतनस्य तस्यानुभावश्रिय साभु जगाधिपस्य ॥

examples.dm: Possessing great generosity, great intelligence, and great power, They have entered the supreme Great Vehicle of the Victors; Clad in great armor, they subdue the illusions of Māra; For that reason, they are truly called "great beings."
examples.gm: Great giving, great intelligence, and great power, Entering into the supreme Great Vehicle of the Jinas, Donning the great armor and subduing the illusions of Mara; Therefore they are proclaimed to be a "great being."
examples.sa: महनायको महतबुद्धि महानुभावो महयान उत्तमजिनान समाधिरूढो । महता सनद्धु नमुचिं शठ धर्षयिष्ये महसत्त्व तेन हि प्रवुच्यति कारणेन ॥

examples.dm: Just as the Guide does not dwell in the unconditioned realm, Likewise, one does not dwell in the conditioned, but practices without a fixed location; In that way, the bodhisattva dwells by not dwelling in any basis; To dwell without a location is what the Victor has taught as "dwelling."
examples.gm: Just as the Guide does not abide in the unconditioned realm, Likewise not abiding in the conditioned, practicing without abiding; Thus the bodhisattva abides in an abiding that is without abiding; Abiding without abiding, this is taught as abiding by the Victorious One.
examples.sa: यथ नायकोऽस्थितकु धातुअसंस्कृताया तथ संस्कृताय अथितो अनिकेतचारी । एवं च स्थानु अथितो स्थित बोधिसत्त्वो अस्थानु स्थानु अयु स्थानु जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Whoever, as a protector, practices this perfection of wisdom, And whoever holds and masters it with devotion, Will not be harmed by poison, weapons, fire, or water; Mara and the factions of Mara will find no opportunity to harm them.
examples.gm: The perfection of wisdom, in which the Protectors practice— Whoever respects, apprehends, and masters it, Will not be harmed by poison, weapons, fire, or water, And Māra and the factions of Māra will find no opportunity against them.
examples.sa: य इमां ग्रहीष्यति पर्यापुणती स नित्यं प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति नाथाः । विष वह्नि शस्त्र उदकं न क्रमाति तस्यो ओतारु मारु न च विन्दति मारपक्षो ॥

examples.dm: Why is that? It is not that I lack respect for the bodily relics; However, because they are completely suffused with wisdom, they are worthy of worship. For example, just as a person who relies on a king receives honor, So too the relics of the Buddha rely upon the Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: "If asked why, it is not that I am disrespectful of the bodily relics; But because they are fully permeated by wisdom, they are worshipped. For example, just as a man relying on a king obtains reverence, The relics of the Buddha rely on the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: किं कारणं न मि शरीरि अगौरवत्वं अपि तू खु प्रज्ञपरिभावित पूजयन्ति । यथ राजनिश्रित नरो लभि सर्वि पूजां तथ प्रज्ञपारमितनिश्रित बुद्धधातुः ॥

examples.dm: Whatever sentient beings there are in this world that provide light, Compared to the light emitted by all of them to illuminate the world, The emergence of a single ray from the sun’s orb is far superior; The light from the host of luminaries cannot match even a fraction of it.
examples.gm: Compared to however many illuminating creatures there are in this world, All emitting their lights in order to illuminate, A single ray of light emitted by the sun's disk is far superior; All the lights of the host of illuminating creatures cannot match it.
examples.sa: यावन्ति लोकि क्वचि जोतिकप्राणभूता ओभासनार्थ प्रभ ओसरयन्ति सर्वे । वरसूर्यमण्डलविनिःसृत एकरश्मी न कला पि ज्योतिकगणे सिय सर्व-आभाः ॥

examples.dm: Therefore, one should train in dedication in this way: Whatever the nature, the source, and the characteristics of that virtue Are as known by those Victors, One should rejoice in it and dedicate it in exactly that same way.
examples.gm: Therefore, one should train in dedicating in this way: Just as those Victors know that virtue— Whatever its aspect, whatever its origin, whatever its defining characteristic— Rejoicing in it, one perfectly dedicates it in exactly that way.
examples.sa: तस्मा हु नामपरिणामन शिक्षितव्या यथ ते जिना कुशल एव प्रजानयन्ति । यज्जातियोऽयं प्रभवो यदलक्षणं च अनुमोदमी तथ तथा परिणामयामि ॥

examples.dm: The wise and luminous bodhisattva who practices in this way, Having severed attachment, moves through the world without clinging, Like the sun shining brightly when freed from the eclipse of Rāhu, Or like a fire that blazes, consuming grass, wood, and forests.
examples.gm: The wise and luminous bodhisattva practicing like that, Having cut off attachment, goes among beings without attachment, Remaining brightly like the sun freed from the eclipse of Rāhu, And like a spreading fire burning grass, trees, and forests.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्तु विदु पण्डितु बोधिसत्त्वो सङ्गा उछिन्नु व्रजते जगती असक्तो । सूर्यो व राहुग्रहमुक्त विरोचमानो अग्नीव युक्त तृणकाष्ठवनं दहाति ॥

examples.dm: Not knowing this, they abandon the root, And in their delusion, they search for the branches and leaves. It is just like finding an elephant and then searching for its tracks; Such is the case for those who have heard the Perfection of Wisdom but still search for other sūtras.
examples.gm: Not knowing thus, having discarded the root, Out of delusion they will search for branches and leaves. It is like finding an elephant but searching for the elephant's footprints; Having heard the perfection of wisdom, searching for other sūtras is just like that.
examples.sa: एवं त मूलमपहाय अजानमानो शाखापलाश परिएषयिष्यन्ति मूढाः । हस्तिं लभित्व यथ हस्तिपदं गवेषे तथ प्रज्ञपारमित श्रुत्व सूत्रान्त एषेत् ॥

examples.dm: The suchness of the world and the suchness of the Arhats, The suchness of the Pratyekabuddhas and the suchness of the Bodhisattvas— These are a single suchness, devoid of entities, a non-dual suchness; The Tathāgata knows this Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: The suchness of the world and the suchness of the arhats, The suchness of the pratyekabuddhas and the suchness of the sons of the Victors: Are oneness, devoid of entities, not other; they are suchness; The perfection of wisdom is known by the Tathāgata.
examples.sa: लोकस्य या तथत या तथतार्हतानां । प्रत्येकबुद्धतथता तथता जिनानाम् । एकैव भावविगता तथता अनन्या प्रज्ञाय पारमित बुद्ध तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: In this way, those endowed with faith who have attained confidence, Do not fail to follow the Mother, the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Likewise, whoever is endowed with faith and has obtained pure trust, But does not follow the mother, the perfection of wisdom,
examples.sa: एमेव श्रद्धसंगतो य प्रसादप्राप्तो प्रज्ञाय पारमित मात्र विवर्जयन्ति । संसारसागर तदा सद संसरन्ति जातीजरामरणशोकतरंगभङ्गे ॥

examples.dm: Those of great renown don the armor of difficult deeds, Which is not the armor of the aggregates, elements, and sense sources. They are free from the concept of the three vehicles and have no grasping; They are irreversible, unwavering, and possess the quality of being imperturbable.
examples.gm: Those endowed with great renown don the armor that is difficult to do; It is not the armor of the aggregates, elements, or sense bases. They are free from the perception of the three vehicles and have no grasping. They are irreversible, unwavering, and of unperturbed nature.
examples.sa: संनाहु दुष्करू महायशु संनहन्ती न च स्कन्धधातु न च आयतनैः सनद्धाः । त्रिभि यानसंज्ञविगता अपरिगृहीता अविवर्तिका अचलिताश्च अकोप्यधर्माः ॥

examples.dm: Thus did the elder Subhūti request of the Protector of the World: "Please explain the signs of the ocean of qualities free from afflictions, And how those of great power do not turn back; O Victor, please grant a prophecy regarding even a mere portion of such qualities."
examples.gm: The elder Subhūti thoroughly requested the Protector of the World: "Ocean of Qualities, please teach the signs of those free from afflictions. How those of great power will not turn back again— Thus, may the Victor explain just a fraction of their qualities."
examples.sa: स्थविरो सुभूति परिपृच्छति लोकनाथं अरणाय लिङ्ग भणही गुणसागराणाम् । अविवर्तिया यथ भवन्ति महानुभावा तां व्याकुरुष्व जिनगुणान प्रदेशमात्रम् ॥

examples.dm: For example, consider a man who indulges in desire and, Having made an appointment with a woman, fails to meet her; However many conceptual thoughts he experiences in his mind throughout a single day, For that many eons, the bodhisattva will achieve attainment.
examples.gm: For example, a man who engages in the phenomena of desire, Having made an appointment with a woman and not meeting her, However many discursive thoughts of his mind operate in a single day, The bodhisattva will gain that many eons.
examples.sa: यथ रागधर्मचरितः पुरुषः स्त्रियाये संकेत कृत्व अलभन्तु विवर्तयेया । यावन्ति चित्तचरिता दिवसेन तस्य तावन्त कल्प अनुबुध्यति बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: If, in a dream, one sees sentient beings dwelling in the three lower realms, And in that very moment makes a prayer to cut the continuum of the lower realms, And pacifies a mass of fire through the power of the blessing of truth— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: In a dream, seeing sentient beings abiding in the three lower realms, In that instant they make aspirations to cut off the stream of the lower realms. Through the blessing of truth, the masses of fire are pacified; They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.
examples.sa: त्रि-अपायप्राप्तु सुपिनस्मि विदित्व सत्त्वान् प्रणिधेति तत्क्षण अपाय उच्छोषयेयम् । सत्याधिष्ठानि प्रशमेति स चाग्निस्कन्धम् अविवर्तियेति अयु व्याकृतु वेदितव्यो ॥

examples.dm: Bodhisattvas who have entered the supreme awakening of a Buddha Should rely on the perfections as their spiritual friends. Those who provide such instruction are the ground of accomplishment; Through these two causes, the awakening of a Buddha is swiftly realized.
examples.gm: Bodhisattvas entered into the supreme awakening of a Buddha Should rely on spiritual friends together with the perfections. Those who teach accordingly, this is the stage of accomplishment; By these two causes, they will swiftly realize the awakening of a Buddha.
examples.sa: बुद्धा य बोधिवरप्रस्थित बोधिसत्त्वा कल्याणमित्र इमि पारमिता निदिष्टाः । ते चानुशासक इयं प्रतिपत्तिभूमी दुवि कारणेन अनुबुध्यति बुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Yogis who practice the supreme perfection of wisdom, Though they generate great compassion, have no perception of sentient beings. At that time, those wise ones become the objects of offering for all the world; They always make meaningful use of the alms of the country.
examples.gm: The yogi practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom, Even when generating great compassion, has no perception of sentient beings; At that time, the wise one becomes a field of generosity for all beings, And always meaningfully fully enjoys the alms of the realm.
examples.sa: चरमाणु प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय योगी महतीं जनेति करुणां न च सत्त्वसंज्ञा । तद भोन्ति सर्वजगती विदु दक्षिणीया सततं अमोघु परिभुञ्जति राष्ट्रपिण्डम् ॥

examples.dm: Both are distant and will become like flesh-eating demons; Both will cause their own commitments to degenerate. How can there be awakening for those who are hostile and devoid of patience? At that time, the Māras and their factions will be delighted.
examples.gm: "Those two will become distant, and they will become like flesh-eating demons; Both will cause their own promises to degenerate. How can there be awakening for those who are hostile and devoid of patience?" At that time, the Māras along with their factions will become joyful.
examples.sa: उभि एति दूरि भविष्यन्ति पिशाचतुल्या उभि एति आत्म करिष्यन्ति प्रतिज्ञहानिम् । दुष्टान क्षान्तिविकलान कुतोऽस्ति बोधि तद मारु तुष्टु भवती नमुचीसपक्षो ॥

examples.dm: For those who have trained in the perfection of wisdom, All the perfections are gathered within this. Just as the sixty-two views are contained within the view of the transitory collection, So too, it is taught that all these perfections are contained within this one.
examples.gm: For those who have trained in the perfection of wisdom, All perfections come to be included herein. Just as the sixty-two views are included within the view of the transitory collection, Likewise, these perfections are taught to be included (herein).
examples.sa: प्रज्ञाय पारमित शिक्षित संस्कृतानां सर्वेष पारमित भोन्तिह संगृहीताः । सत्कायदृष्टि यथ षष्टि दुवे च दृष्टी अन्तर्गतास्तथमि पारमिता भवन्ति ॥

examples.dm: For example, a phantom buddha performs the deeds of a buddha, Yet not even a trace of pride arises in that performance. Likewise, the bodhisattva who is skilled in the practice of wisdom Displays all activities just like a magical emanation.
examples.gm: For example, an emanation of a Buddha performs the deeds of a Buddha, And in doing so, not even a little pride arises; Likewise, the wise bodhisattvas practicing wisdom Demonstrate all activities like an emanation or an illusion.
examples.sa: यथ बुद्ध निर्मित करोति च बुद्धकार्यं न च तस्युपद्यति मदो करमाणु किंचित् । एमेव प्रज्ञचरितो विदु बोधिसत्त्वो दर्शेति सर्व क्रिय निर्मितमायतुल्यम् ॥

examples.dm: Those who wish to attain the supreme qualities of all beings, To touch the most marvelous and supreme primordial wisdom of the Buddha, And to bestow the most excellent and holy gift of Dharma, Should rely upon this supreme state of the benefactors.
examples.gm: To go to the supreme qualities of all sentient beings, And to touch the supremely marvelous, supreme Buddha-wisdom, Whosoever desires to give the supreme, holy gift of Dharma, Rely on this supreme dwelling of those who bring benefit!
examples.sa: यो सर्वसत्त्वगुण-अग्रतु गन्तुकामो अग्रं स्पृशेय परमाद्भुत बुद्धज्ञानम् । अग्रं ददेय वर उत्तमधर्मदानम् इमु अग्रु सेवतु विहारु हितंकराणाम् ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, the bodhisattvas who possess supreme qualities, Diligent in yoga and abiding in meditative concentration and absorption, Dwell once again in the desire realm without attachment; Like a lotus in the water, they are not stained by the qualities of the foolish.
examples.gm: Similarly, those who hold the supreme qualities of a bodhisattva, Exerting themselves in yoga and abiding in the samādhis of the dhyānas, Again abide in the desire realm without attachment; Like a lotus in water, they do not abide in the dharmas of fools.
examples.sa: एमेव ते गुणधरा वरबोधिसत्त्वा ध्याने समाधि विहरित्व प्रयुक्तयोगी । पुन कामधातुस्थित भोन्ति अनोपलिप्ता पद्मेव वारिणि अनिश्रित बालधर्मे ॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, even though they are intensely engaged with the five sensory qualities— Forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and textures— If they take joy in the Bodhicitta that is free from the vehicles of the Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas, Know that these heroes are always in meditative equipoise.
examples.gm: Moreover, forms and sounds, and likewise smells and tastes, Touches, and the five qualities of desire, even if they exert themselves in these, If they are free from the vehicles of the arhat and pratyekabuddha and delight in the mind of awakening, The hero should be known to be constantly in meditative equipoise.
examples.sa: किंचापि रूपम् अपि शब्द तथैव गन्धो रस स्पर्श कामगुण पञ्चभि युक्त भोगी । रहप्रत्ययान विगतोऽनन्तबोधिसत्त्वो सततं समाहितु प्रजानयितव्य शूरो ॥

examples.dm: When they have no perception of a body, a mind, or a sentient being, And having turned back from perceptions, they practice the non-dual Dharma— This is what the Benefactor called the perfection of perseverance For those who desire the supreme, undeterred, and peaceful awakening.
examples.gm: Whenever there is no perception of body, mind, and sentient beings, And having completely turned away from perception, one practices the non-dual dharma, For one who desires the supreme, unwaning, peaceful awakening, This was taught by the Benefactor to be the perfection of diligence.
examples.sa: यस्मिन् न कायु न पि चित्त न सत्त्वसंज्ञा संज्ञाविवर्ति स्थितु अद्वयधर्मचारी । अयु वीर्यपारमित उक्त हितंकरेण आकाङ्क्षमाणु शिवम् अच्युतम् अग्रबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: If, for ten million eons, one practices the ten paths of virtuous action, Yet generates a desire for the state of an Arhat or a Pratyekabuddha, At that moment, one’s ethical discipline is flawed and has degenerated; That generation of such a thought is far weightier than even a formal defeat.
examples.gm: Even if one practices the ten paths of virtuous action for ten million aeons, If one generates the desire for the state of an arhat or solitary realizer, At that time, one's discipline becomes flawed and one's discipline degenerates; Generating that mind is much heavier even than a defeat.
examples.sa: यदि कल्पकोटि दशभी कुशलैः पथेभिश् चरमाणु प्रत्ययरहत्वस्पृहां जनेति । तद खण्डशीलु भवते अपि छिद्रशीलो पाराजिको गुरुतरो अयु चित्तुपादो ॥

examples.dm: Those who grasp at the actual perception of a self and hold things as "mine" are attached; How could fools like these ever have the intention to give? Those who are stingy will be born in the realm of hungry ghosts; Even if they are born as humans, they will be destitute at that time.
examples.gm: Perceiving a self, one is attached to things through grasping them as "mine"; How could fools have the mind of generosity? Miserly ones will be born in the realm of hungry ghosts; Or even if they are born as humans, they will then be impoverished.
examples.sa: अहसंज्ञतस्तु ममता भवते च रागो कुतु त्यागबुद्धि भविष्यति सा मुहानाम् । मात्सर्य प्रेत भवते उपपद्ययाती अथवा मनुष्य तद भोति दरिद्ररूपो ॥

examples.dm: Even a massive heap of ordinary glass trinkets Is outshone by a single precious lapis lazuli gem; Likewise, all the vast heaps of generosity of all beings Are outshone by a bodhisattva who rejoices.
examples.gm: Even a great heap of imitation glass jewels Is completely outshone by a single precious lapis lazuli; Likewise, all the vast heaps of giving of all beings Are outshone by the rejoicing bodhisattva.
examples.sa: काचस्य वा मणिन राशि सिया महन्तो वैडूर्यरत्न अभिभोति स सर्व एको । एमेव सर्वजगती पृथु दानस्कन्धो अभिभोति सर्वपरिणामकु बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: The eighth chapter: teaching the Dharmakāya. One fully embraces the pure realm and the purity of sentient beings; One fully embraces the lineage of the Buddha and the lineage of the Dharma; Likewise, one fully embraces the lineage of the Saṅgha and all phenomena.
examples.gm: Chapter Eight: Teaching the Dharmakāya. Fully upholds perfectly pure fields and pure sentient beings; Fully upholds the Buddha lineage and also the Dharma lineage; Likewise fully upholds the Sangha lineage and all dharmas.
